rows.requirement: A capability MUST declare a schema URL; services and payment handlers declare one where their transport or handler defines it. A spec URL is now optional (MAY) rather than required for every entity.
rows.quote:
A capability **MUST** declare a `schema`; services and payment handlers declare
one where their transport or handler defines it. Each entity **MAY** also
declare a `spec` URL (human-readable documentation).
rows.notes: REWORDED, flagged for review (security-relevant): OLD quote (overview.md#L82, old section '#### Spec URL Binding'): "The `spec` and `schema` fields are **REQUIRED** for all capabilities." — BOTH spec and schema were mandatory for every capability. NEW quote (new section '#### Authority Binding'): schema is MUST for capabilities (and conditionally for services/payment handlers), while spec is downgraded to MAY — explicitly optional, described elsewhere in the same section as documentation that is 'not part of the machine trust path'. This is a genuine normative relaxation (REQUIRED -> optional for spec), not a cosmetic reword. Keyword updated from the old ad-hoc 'REQUIRED' to 'MUST' to match the new text's primary clause (schema). See OVR-003 for the paired origin-binding change.

rows.requirement: For any entity that declares a remote schema URL, the origin of that schema URL MUST match the namespace authority derived from its reverse-domain name (the spec URL is explicitly exempted from this binding in 2026-08-25)
rows.quote:
Authority binding applies to every entity with a remote `schema`: a declared `schema`
URL's origin **MUST** match the namespace authority in its name.
rows.notes: REWORDED, flagged for review (security-relevant): OLD quote (overview.md#L83): "The `spec` and `schema` fields are **REQUIRED** for all capabilities. The origin ... of these URLs **MUST** match the namespace authority:" — origin-authority binding applied to BOTH the spec and schema URLs of capabilities. NEW quote narrows this explicitly to the schema URL only ('every entity with a remote schema'), and a few lines later the same new section states outright: "The `spec` URL is documentation, not part of the machine trust path, so its origin is **not** authority-bound: it **MUST** be `https` but **MAY** be served from any host." Binding also now extends beyond capabilities to any entity with a remote schema (services, payment handlers), broader than the old capability-only scope. Net effect: spec URLs are EXEMPTED from the provenance/origin check that used to apply to them; schema-origin binding is unchanged in effect but now framed as 'provenance, not trust'. Cross-cuts OVR-002 (spec also downgraded from REQUIRED to MAY there).

rows.requirement: Arithmetic over quantity/amount values MUST be exact; an implementation that cannot produce an exact, in-range result MUST surface an error rather than emit, display, or act on an approximate or wrapped value.
rows.quote:
Arithmetic over these values **MUST** be exact. Within the wire range,
IEEE 754 binary64 — a JavaScript `Number` from `JSON.parse` — holds every
integer exactly; products such as `amount × quantity` can exceed 64 bits, so
use wider or arbitrary-precision integers, or overflow checks. An
implementation that cannot produce an exact, in-range result **MUST**
surface an error rather than emit, display, or act on an approximate or
wrapped value.

rows.requirement: A tied precedence score means two same-type policies cover a node at the same depth and precision, an authoring error; a Business MUST NOT publish such a collision.
rows.quote:
4. When the greatest score is shared, the outcome is **undefined**. A tie
   requires two policies to cover the node at the same depth and precision;

   is an authoring error, not an artifact of path targeting: naming the node by

rows.notes: New row (Negotiation Protocol > Platform Requirements, item 3). Restates the Authority Binding enforcement duty (CAP-009) specifically as a platform-side negotiation-protocol step; kept distinct from CAP-009 because it is the platform's own enumerated Negotiation Protocol obligation, addressed to a different actor context (protocol requirements checklist vs. the Authority Binding section's Enforcement subsection).

rows.requirement: Negotiation Protocol, Platform Requirements item 4 (Schema Resolution): Platforms MUST fetch and compose schemas for negotiated capabilities before making requests.
rows.quote:
4. **Schema Resolution**: Platforms **MUST** fetch and compose schemas for
    negotiated capabilities before making requests.
rows.notes: New row (Negotiation Protocol > Platform Requirements, item 4).

rows.requirement: Negotiation Protocol, Business Requirements item 1 (Profile Resolution): upon receiving a request with a platform profile URI, businesses MUST fetch and validate the platform profile unless already cached.

rows.quote:

    platform and business capabilities.
rows.notes: New row (Negotiation Protocol > Business Requirements, item 2).

rows.requirement: When using Streamable HTTP transport for MCP, servers MUST return the corresponding HTTP status code (e.g. 429 for rate limit) alongside the JSON-RPC error; the HTTP status code is the primary signal for error type.

rows.requirement: Business-to-platform webhooks MUST be signed.

rows.notes: New row (Authentication Mechanisms). Cross-references signatures.md#when-signatures-apply for the full signing requirement; kept here as its own row since this is the overview-level statement of the webhook-signing obligation, distinct from the signatures.md mechanics rows.

rows.requirement: For a WBA-shape signature resolved via Signature-Agent, the signature MUST satisfy the WBA agent-signature requirements (draft-meunier-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00 §4.2), and the Signature-Agent member value MUST be an HTTPS URL.

      requirements in
      [draft-meunier-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-meunier-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol/00/)
      §4.2 (see [WBA Interop](../signatures.md#wba-interop) for the
      signer-side shape). The member value **MUST** be an HTTPS URL.
rows.notes: New row (Identity Resolution Algorithm, step 1, Signature-Agent sub-bullet).

rows.requirement: For a WBA-shape signature (tag="web-bot-auth"), the verifier MUST also confirm that keyid equals the RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of the matched JWK, binding the advertised key identity to its bytes; if it fails, the signature is skipped.
rows.quote:
(`tag="web-bot-auth"`), the verifier **MUST** also confirm `keyid`
   equals the [RFC 7638](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7638) SHA-256
   thumbprint of the matched JWK — the WBA architecture draft §4.2
   requires this, binding the advertised key identity to its bytes. If
   it fails, skip this signature.
rows.notes: New row (Identity Resolution Algorithm, step 4).

`algorithm_unsupported`, or related error) only when every signature
has been skipped or fails verification.
rows.notes: New row (Identity Resolution Algorithm, rejection condition).

rows.requirement: Implementations MUST treat the request as a single authenticated identity only when the Signature-Agent and UCP-Agent URLs are the same after normalization; otherwise they are distinct identities and policy decides whether either suffices.
rows.notes: New row (Identity Resolution Algorithm, Authenticated identity).

4. Businesses **MUST** include the negotiated protocol version in
